$description: Serupa's own tokens: a hex color palette, alias colors in six themes, and the type, spacing, sizing, border, shadow, motion, layout, filter, transform and opacity scales behind every utility class.

families.sans: Inter, "Inter Fallback", "Noto Sans Arabic", "Noto Sans Hebrew", "Noto Sans Devanagari", "Noto Sans Thai", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif
families.serif: Georgia, Cambria, "Times New Roman", Times, serif
families.mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace

groups.name: Type scale

scripts.note: Noto Sans Arabic is in the sans stack. Marks above and below the letters need a taller line: 1.6 at the least.
Noto Sans Devanagari is in the sans stack. Vowel signs above the headline and below the letters need 1.5 at the least.
Noto Sans Thai is in the sans stack. Tone marks stack above vowels: 1.5 at the least (the font's own height is 1.51).
Han characters are drawn differently in each language, so the font follows lang. Square characters read best with 1.5 at the least.
As Japanese. After Simplified Chinese, so zh-TW wins over zh.

primary.$description: Alias. Brand color: primary buttons, links, selected states. Light themes: brand 600 (emerald 700) with white text; dark themes: brand 400 with brand-950 text. More contrast: brand 800 / brand 300, 7:1+ on `surface` and `primary-subtle`.

primary-hover.$description: Alias. Hover / pressed state of `primary` (one step darker in light themes, lighter in dark). More contrast: brand 900 / brand 200.

primary-subtle.$description: Alias. Brand tint for selected rows and badges (brand 50 light, brand 950 dark).

on-primary.$description: Alias. Text and icons on `primary` fills (white in light themes, brand 950 in dark).

secondary.$description: Alias. Secondary button fill; hover fill for outline and ghost buttons.

highlight.$description: The keyboard-highlighted item in a list: Menu items, Combobox and TimePicker options, the Sidebar's current page. One step stronger than `secondary` in light (about 1.3:1 on `surface`); in dark it shares `secondary`'s zinc-700 (1.7:1 on `surface`, 1.4:1 on `surface-overlay`), so a `primary` bar keeps 3:1 on it in every brand, paired with a 2px `primary` bar at the item's start. Text on it keeps 4.5:1.

pressed.$description: Alias. The fill while a row, tab, day or page button is held down (`:active`): one step past its hover. `text` keeps 7:1+ on it.

surface.$description: Alias. Page and card background (white light, zinc-900 dark).

surface-muted.$description: Alias. Secondary panels, sidebars, table headers.

surface-raised.$description: Alias. A raised card (Card `elevated`). One step up from `surface` in dark, where a shadow doesn't show.

surface-overlay.$description: Alias. Anything in the top layer: Menu, Popover, Dialog, Drawer, Toast and the Combobox, DatePicker and TimePicker lists.

field.$description: Alias. Background of text inputs, selects and other form fields.

field-readonly.$description: Alias. Background of a read-only or disabled form field: a step flatter than `field` (zinc-50 in light, the page's zinc-900 in dark), so it reads as not editable while its `field-border` still outlines it.

field-border.$description: Alias. Border of form fields. 3:1+ against `field` and `surface` in every theme, as WCAG 1.4.11 requires for a control's boundary.

placeholder.$description: Alias. Placeholder text in form fields (4.5:1+ on `field`). Placeholders are hints, never labels.

overlay.$description: Alias. The dimmed backdrop behind dialogs and drawers (zinc-900 at 50% in light themes, zinc-950 at 70% in dark).

surface-inverse.$description: Alias. Contrasting blocks: tooltips, inverse banners.

text.$description: Alias. Body text and headings on `surface`.

text-muted.$description: Alias. Secondary text, captions, placeholders (4.5:1+ on `surface` in every theme).

border-strong.$description: Alias. Emphasised dividers and outlines. Form fields use `field-border`, which meets the 3:1 a control boundary needs.

border-raised.$description: Alias. A raised card's edge: invisible in light (white on white), a 1px lighter edge in dark.

border-overlay.$description: Alias. The edge of a top-layer surface. In dark it is one step stronger than `border`, so a menu stands off the page.

focus-ring.$description: Alias. Keyboard focus outline, in the brand hue (3:1+ on `surface` in every theme). More contrast: brand 700 / brand 300.

success.$description: Alias. Success icons and fills (3:1). For success text use `success-text`.

success-text.$description: Alias. Success text on `surface`, `surface-muted` and `success-subtle` (4.5:1+ in every theme).

warning.$description: Alias. Warning icons and fills; put dark text on it. For warning text use `warning-text`.

warning-text.$description: Alias. Warning text on `surface`, `surface-muted` and `warning-subtle` (4.5:1+ in every theme).

danger.$description: Alias. Errors, destructive buttons; white text on it (4.8:1). For error text on dark surfaces use `red-400`.

on-danger.$description: Alias. Text and icons on `danger` fills.

danger-text.$description: Alias. Destructive text and icons on `surface`, `danger-subtle` and its hover (5.3:1+ in every theme).

danger-subtle-hover.$description: Alias. Hover fill for destructive secondary, outline and ghost buttons.

danger-border.$description: Alias. Border of a destructive outline button.

info-text.$description: Alias. Info text on `surface`, `surface-muted` and `info-subtle` (4.5:1+ in every theme).

link-visited.$description: Alias. A visited link in reading content (Prose): a shade apart from primary, 4.5:1+ on `surface` and `surface-muted` in every theme.

spacing.$description: The spacing scale: 1 unit = 0.25rem (4px). Used by padding, margin, gap, width and height utilities.

radius.$description: The corner radius scale: xs is 2px, sm is 4px.

rounded.$description: `rounded`: 4px. Same as `rounded-sm`; kept for older code.

rounded-full.$description: `rounded-full`: Pills and circles: avatars, badges, toggles.

shadow.$description: Shadow scales: box shadows (2xs to 2xl), inner shadows and text shadows. Black at 5–25% opacity; a color class swaps the black.

text-shadow-2xs.$description: `text-shadow-2xs`. Crisp edge on small text over images.

borders.$description: Border and outline widths and outline offsets (in px), plus SVG stroke widths (unitless, in the SVG's own units). Colors come from the palette and alias tokens; radius is in its own group.

outline-offset-2.$description: `outline-offset-2`. Gap between an element and its focus outline.

focus-ring-width.$description: The focus ring's width: `outline: var(--focus-ring-width) solid var(--focus-ring)`. Every component's focus ring uses it. A third thicker (3px) with more contrast.

focus-ring-offset.$description: The transparent gap between an element and its focus ring (`outline-offset`). Inset rings, where an outline would be clipped, use 0.

stroke-width-1.$description: `stroke-1`. Hairline outlines and dividers in illustrations.

stroke-width-2.$description: `stroke-2`. The usual weight for outline icons (as in Lucide/Heroicons).

stroke-width-3.$description: `stroke-3`. Bold strokes for large or emphasized icons.

stroke-width-4.$description: `stroke-4`. Heavy strokes for charts and display graphics.

typography.$description: Font weight, letter spacing, line height, font stretch, underline thickness and offset, line clamp and tab size. Font families and sizes live in the Typography styles.

font-thin.$description: `font-thin` (100). Available for special cases (marketing, display type, data viz); not used by components.

font-extralight.$description: `font-extralight` (200). Available for special cases (marketing, display type, data viz); not used by components.

font-light.$description: `font-light` (300). Available for special cases (marketing, display type, data viz); not used by components.

font-normal.$description: Default · Regular (400): body text, long-form reading, inputs.

font-medium.$description: Default · Medium (500): buttons, labels, tabs, table headers, emphasis inside body text.

font-semibold.$description: Default · Semibold (600): headings and titles at every size.

font-bold.$description: `font-bold` (700). Available for special cases (marketing, display type, data viz); not used by components.

font-extrabold.$description: `font-extrabold` (800). Available for special cases (marketing, display type, data viz); not used by components.

font-black.$description: `font-black` (900). Available for special cases (marketing, display type, data viz); not used by components.

font-stretch-ultra-condensed.$description: `font-stretch-ultra-condensed` (50%). Only for fonts with width variants; Inter has none, so the browser picks the closest.

font-stretch-extra-condensed.$description: `font-stretch-extra-condensed` (62.5%). Only for fonts with width variants; Inter has none, so the browser picks the closest.

font-stretch-condensed.$description: `font-stretch-condensed` (75%). Only for fonts with width variants; Inter has none, so the browser picks the closest.

font-stretch-semi-condensed.$description: `font-stretch-semi-condensed` (87.5%). Only for fonts with width variants; Inter has none, so the browser picks the closest.

font-stretch-normal.$description: `font-stretch-normal` (100%). Only for fonts with width variants; Inter has none, so the browser picks the closest.

font-stretch-semi-expanded.$description: `font-stretch-semi-expanded` (112.5%). Only for fonts with width variants; Inter has none, so the browser picks the closest.

font-stretch-expanded.$description: `font-stretch-expanded` (125%). Only for fonts with width variants; Inter has none, so the browser picks the closest.

font-stretch-extra-expanded.$description: `font-stretch-extra-expanded` (150%). Only for fonts with width variants; Inter has none, so the browser picks the closest.

font-stretch-ultra-expanded.$description: `font-stretch-ultra-expanded` (200%). Only for fonts with width variants; Inter has none, so the browser picks the closest.

line-clamp-1.$description: `line-clamp-1`: cut text after 1 line with an ellipsis.

line-clamp-2.$description: `line-clamp-2`: cut text after 2 lines with an ellipsis.

line-clamp-3.$description: `line-clamp-3`: cut text after 3 lines with an ellipsis.

line-clamp-4.$description: `line-clamp-4`: cut text after 4 lines with an ellipsis.

line-clamp-5.$description: `line-clamp-5`: cut text after 5 lines with an ellipsis.

line-clamp-6.$description: `line-clamp-6`: cut text after 6 lines with an ellipsis.

tab-2.$description: `tab-2`: tab characters as wide as 2 spaces (code blocks).

tab-4.$description: `tab-4`: tab characters as wide as 4 spaces (code blocks).

tab-8.$description: `tab-8`: tab characters as wide as 8 spaces (code blocks).

layout.$description: Layout scales: breakpoints (min-width, mobile first; the container's max-width snaps to them), z-index layers, aspect ratios and column widths.

screen-sm.$description: `sm:` breakpoint, `@media (min-width: 640px)`. Large phones in landscape, small tablets. Container max-width 640px.

screen-lg.$description: `lg:` breakpoint, `@media (min-width: 1024px)`. Laptops and small desktops. Container max-width 1024px.

z-10.$description: `z-10`. Local stacking, step 1: lift an element over its siblings, such as a badge over an avatar.

z-50.$description: `z-50`. Local stacking, step 5. For page layers (menus, dialogs, toasts) use the named layers.

z-sticky.$description: Layer: Sticky headers and toolbars. Use the named layers instead of numbers so stacking stays consistent.

z-dropdown.$description: Layer: Dropdown menus and select lists. Use the named layers instead of numbers so stacking stays consistent.

z-overlay.$description: Layer: The `overlay` backdrop behind a dialog. Use the named layers instead of numbers so stacking stays consistent.

z-modal.$description: Layer: Dialogs and drawers, above their backdrop. Use the named layers instead of numbers so stacking stays consistent.

z-popover.$description: Layer: Popovers opened from inside a dialog. Use the named layers instead of numbers so stacking stays consistent.

z-toast.$description: Layer: Toast notifications, above dialogs. Use the named layers instead of numbers so stacking stays consistent.

z-tooltip.$description: Layer: Tooltips, above everything. Use the named layers instead of numbers so stacking stays consistent.

columns-3xs.$description: `columns-3xs`: as many columns as fit at least 256px wide.

columns-2xs.$description: `columns-2xs`: as many columns as fit at least 288px wide.

columns-xs.$description: `columns-xs`: as many columns as fit at least 320px wide.

columns-sm.$description: `columns-sm`: as many columns as fit at least 384px wide.

columns-md.$description: `columns-md`: as many columns as fit at least 448px wide.

columns-lg.$description: `columns-lg`: as many columns as fit at least 512px wide.

columns-xl.$description: `columns-xl`: as many columns as fit at least 576px wide.

columns-2xl.$description: `columns-2xl`: as many columns as fit at least 672px wide.

columns-3xl.$description: `columns-3xl`: as many columns as fit at least 768px wide.

columns-4xl.$description: `columns-4xl`: as many columns as fit at least 896px wide.

columns-5xl.$description: `columns-5xl`: as many columns as fit at least 1024px wide.

columns-6xl.$description: `columns-6xl`: as many columns as fit at least 1152px wide.

columns-7xl.$description: `columns-7xl`: as many columns as fit at least 1280px wide.

sizing.$description: The sizing scale for width, min/max-width, height, min/max-height, inline-size, min/max-inline-size, block-size and min/max-block-size. Numbers use the spacing scale (w-4 = spacing-4); named sizes use the container scale; fractions and keywords below.

container-xs.$description: 320px, used by `w-xs`, `min-w-xs`, `max-w-xs`, `inline-xs`, `min-inline-xs`, `max-inline-xs`. Small dialogs, popover cards.

container-sm.$description: 384px, used by `w-sm`, `min-w-sm`, `max-w-sm`, `inline-sm`, `min-inline-sm`, `max-inline-sm`. Sign-in forms, narrow dialogs.

container-xl.$description: 576px, used by `w-xl`, `min-w-xl`, `max-w-xl`, `inline-xl`, `min-inline-xl`, `max-inline-xl`. Side panels, form pages.

container-2xl.$description: 672px, used by `w-2xl`, `min-w-2xl`, `max-w-2xl`, `inline-2xl`, `min-inline-2xl`, `max-inline-2xl`. Settings pages, long forms.

container-3xl.$description: 768px, used by `w-3xl`, `min-w-3xl`, `max-w-3xl`, `inline-3xl`, `min-inline-3xl`, `max-inline-3xl`. Article and document bodies with images.

container-5xl.$description: 1024px, used by `w-5xl`, `min-w-5xl`, `max-w-5xl`, `inline-5xl`, `min-inline-5xl`, `max-inline-5xl`. Dashboards with a sidebar.

container-7xl.$description: 1280px, used by `w-7xl`, `min-w-7xl`, `max-w-7xl`, `inline-7xl`, `min-inline-7xl`, `max-inline-7xl`. Marketing and full app shells.

container-prose.$description: `max-w-prose`: about 65 characters per line, the comfortable reading width for body text.

sizing-auto.$description: Let the browser decide (not for max-*).

sizing-dvh.$description: Dynamic viewport height: tracks the mobile browser bar.

sizing-max.$description: Widest the content wants, no wrapping.

sizing-fit.$description: Content size, capped by the space available.

control-height-sm.$description: Height of small controls (24px): `sm` buttons, compact inputs. The WCAG 2.2 AA minimum target size.

control-height-md.$description: Height of default controls (32px): buttons, inputs and selects line up at this height.

control-height-lg.$description: Height of large controls (44px), the comfortable touch target (WCAG 2.5.5).

flexGrid.$description: Flexbox and grid values that aren't on another scale. gap, basis and auto-cols/rows numbers use the spacing scale; basis also uses the container scale and fractions.

flex-auto.$description: `flex-auto`: grow and shrink from the content size.

filters.$description: Filter and backdrop-filter scales: blur, drop shadows, brightness, contrast, saturation and hue rotation. Grayscale, invert and sepia need no tokens (0–100%); backdrop-opacity uses the opacity group.

blur-sm.$description: `blur-sm`, `backdrop-blur-sm`. Frosted glass behind menus and popovers (`backdrop-blur-sm`).

blur-md.$description: `blur-md`, `backdrop-blur-md`. Frosted glass behind sticky headers and sheets.

drop-shadow-xs.$description: `drop-shadow-xs`. Barely-there lift for icons and small shapes.

drop-shadow-sm.$description: `drop-shadow-sm`. Icons and logos on a surface.

transforms.$description: Transform scales: perspective, rotation, scale, skew and zoom. translate uses the spacing scale; origins, backface and transform-style are keywords.

perspective-dramatic.$description: `perspective-dramatic`. Strong, close-up 3D: card flips at small sizes.

scale-90.$description: `scale-90`, `-scale-90`, `scale-x-90`, `scale-y-90`, `scale-z-90`. Enter animations for menus and dialogs.

scale-97.$description: `scale-97`, `-scale-97`, `scale-x-97`, `scale-y-97`, `scale-z-97`. Pressed buttons and small controls (Button's press feedback).

scale-105.$description: `scale-105`, `-scale-105`, `scale-x-105`, `scale-y-105`, `scale-z-105`. Hover lift on cards and images.

opacity.$description: The opacity scale, 0–100% in 5% steps: `opacity-*` and `backdrop-opacity-*`.

opacity-0.$description: `opacity-0`, `backdrop-opacity-0`. Hidden but still in the layout.

opacity-disabled.$description: `opacity-disabled`. Every disabled control and item (50%). Set it once to change how disabled looks everywhere.

transitions.$description: Motion: transition durations (`duration-*`) and delays (`delay-*`), easings (`ease-*`), the property lists that transitions animate (`transition*`), and animations (`animate-*`). Components use the roles (`motion-press`, `motion-hover`, `motion-enter-*`, `motion-exit-*`, `motion-loop-*`, `ease-enter`, `ease-exit`, `ease-move`, `ease-settle`, `ease-pop`, `ease-spring`, `motion-stagger`), which name what moves rather than how long it takes. 150ms with `ease-in-out` is the default for UI state changes.

duration-100.$description: Presses and small exits: a button held down, a tooltip leaving.

duration-150.$description: Default: hover and focus colors, and small surfaces entering (tooltips, popovers, menus, date pickers).

duration-200.$description: Medium surfaces entering: dialogs and toasts.

duration-300.$description: Large surfaces entering: drawers and sheets.

duration-1200.$description: Long loops, such as the pixel loader (1.2s). Decorative only.

delay-50.$description: One step of a stagger: the gap between list items arriving (`motion-stagger`).

ease-in.$description: Starts slow: elements leaving the screen.

ease-out.$description: Ends slow: elements entering (menus, dialogs, toasts). The same curve as ease-out-quart: most of the travel at once, then a long landing.

ease-in-out.$description: Default: state changes that stay on screen (hover, toggles). The same curve as ease-in-out-cubic: a clear start and a clear finish.

ease-out-quart.$description: Decelerates firmly: quick off the mark, a long smooth landing. Surfaces entering (`ease-enter`).

ease-out-expo.$description: Decelerates hard: almost all of the travel at once, then a long glide to rest. Values arriving and slides let go (`ease-settle`).

ease-in-cubic.$description: Accelerates gently from a standstill: something drifting off. Slower to get going than `ease-in`, so not for closing surfaces.

ease-in-quart.$description: Accelerates firmly: something thrown off screen.

ease-in-expo.$description: Accelerates hard: barely moves, then gone. Rarely right for UI.

ease-in-out-cubic.$description: Smooth start and finish: something that stays on screen and changes (`ease-move`).

ease-in-out-quart.$description: A pronounced start and finish: a large panel or page-level change.

ease-in-out-expo.$description: The most pronounced start and finish: a deliberate, dramatic move. Use rarely.

ease-out-back.$description: Decelerates past the end by about 4%, then comes back: something small popping into place (`ease-pop`).

ease-spring-soft.$description: A damped spring (damping ratio 0.85) that barely overshoots, written as `linear()`: something released that comes to rest naturally. Generated by `tools/tokens/spring.mjs`.

ease-spring-snappy.$description: A damped spring (damping ratio 0.6) that overshoots by about 9% and settles, written as `linear()`: a press let go springing back (`ease-spring`). Generated by `tools/tokens/spring.mjs`.

ease-elastic.$description: A loose spring (damping ratio 0.3) that overshoots by about 37% and wobbles a few times before it settles, written as `linear()`. Only for small, rare, celebratory moments (`ease-celebrate`), never for surfaces or anything people do over and over. Generated by `tools/tokens/spring.mjs`.

motion-press.$description: A press: a control answering while it's held down (Button scales down).

motion-release.$description: A press let go: the control springing back to its size with `ease-spring`. Longer than the press, because a spring spends its end settling; it is back in place in about a third of this.

motion-hover.$description: Hover and focus changes: colors, borders and shadows on a control that stays put.

motion-enter-sm.$description: A small surface appearing: tooltips, popovers, menus, date pickers.

motion-enter-md.$description: A medium surface appearing: dialogs and toasts.

motion-enter-lg.$description: A large surface appearing: drawers and sheets.

motion-exit-sm.$description: A small surface leaving. An exit takes about two thirds of its enter, so what was closed gets out of the way.

motion-exit-md.$description: A medium surface leaving: dialogs and toasts.

motion-exit-lg.$description: A large surface leaving: drawers and sheets.

motion-change-sm.$description: A small part changing in place: a chevron turning, a slider thumb growing, a dot widening, a row gliding to its place.

motion-change-md.$description: A panel opening or collapsing in place, or an indicator sliding to the selected option: Accordion, Sidebar, SegmentedControl, Tabs.

motion-change-lg.$description: Something travelling far on screen: a progress or meter fill moving to its value, a carousel slide.

motion-loop-spinner.$description: One turn of a spinner, the one spinner speed: Loader's ring (and so Button, Badge and SearchInput), Switch and the circular Progress while they load. Under reduced motion they stand still and breathe over twice this.

motion-loop-placeholder.$description: One pass of a loading placeholder's pulse: Image while it loads.

motion-loop-blink.$description: One blink of a text caret: PinInput.

motion-loop-progress.$description: One pass of an indeterminate progress bar.

motion-ripple.$description: A press ripple spreading out from the pointer: Button and Badge.

motion-ripple-fade.$description: A press ripple fading once it has spread.

motion-stagger.$description: The gap between items of a group arriving one after another, for a group seen now and then (a page's cards, a first list of results), never one opened over and over (menu items, toasts). Each item waits its index times this.

motion-stagger-limit.$description: The longest any item of a staggered group waits, so a long list still arrives within a moment: items past the sixth arrive together.

motion-sequence.$description: The offset between the steps of one entrance, so they read as a sequence: a dialog or drawer’s backdrop starts, then its panel. Exits don’t sequence; everything leaves together.

ease-enter.$description: Something appearing: quick off the mark, then a long smooth landing.

ease-exit.$description: Something leaving: at full speed from the first frame, then easing off as it fades, so a closed surface is out of the way at once. An ease-in starts slowly, and the first frames after a close are the ones people watch.

ease-move.$description: Something that stays on screen and changes: a thumb sliding, a panel resizing, a color changing. A smooth start and finish.

ease-settle.$description: Something arriving at a new value or let go by the hand: a fill, a slide, a drawer dropped. Most of the travel at once, then a long glide to rest.

ease-pop.$description: Something small popping into place: a check mark, a count, a dot. Overshoots a touch, then settles.

ease-spring.$description: A press let go springing back, or a thumb or indicator landing: a real spring that overshoots and settles. Pair it with a duration about twice the motion it answers (a press of `motion-press` springs back over `motion-change-md`).

ease-fling.$description: Something the hand let go of mid-motion carrying on to rest: a drawer or carousel slide flicked. It starts at three times its average speed, so a settle timed as 3 × distance ÷ the hand’s speed starts exactly at that speed and slows from there (`settleTime()` in the components).

ease-celebrate.$description: A small, rare moment worth celebrating: a success check landing, a count bumping, an item snapping into its slot after a drag. Wobbles, then settles. Give it about three times the motion it answers (`motion-change-lg` or longer) so the wobble reads, and never use it for menus, dialogs, page moves or repeated actions. Off under reduced motion.

transition.$value: opacity, box-shadow, transform, translate, scale, rotate, filter, -webkit-backdrop-filter, backdrop-filter, display, content-visibility, overlay, pointer-events
transition.$description: `transition` (default) animates `transition-colors` plus these: opacity, shadow, transforms, filters and discrete properties like display.

transition-colors.$value: color, background-color, border-color, outline-color, text-decoration-color, fill, stroke, --dk-gradient-from, --dk-gradient-via, --dk-gradient-to
transition-colors.$description: `transition-colors`: hover and focus color changes, gradients included.

transition-transform.$description: `transition-transform`: moves, scales and rotations, including the translate/scale/rotate classes.

transition-all.$description: Avoid in components: it also animates layout properties.

animate-spin-reduced.$description: `animate-spin` when the viewer prefers reduced motion: the same turn, three times slower. Applied automatically.

animate-ping.$description: `animate-ping`: a radar ping behind a notification dot or live badge.

animate-enter.$description: `animate-enter`: content arriving, fading in as it rises a little into place. With `stagger` on the parent, the items arrive one after another. Under reduced motion it only fades.

fontSize.$description: Font sizes and the line height that goes with each, read by the `text-*` classes and by components. The same values make up the "Font size" type styles.

text-xs--line-height.$description: The line height that goes with `text-xs`.

text-sm--line-height.$description: The line height that goes with `text-sm`.

text-base--line-height.$description: The line height that goes with `text-base`.

text-lg--line-height.$description: The line height that goes with `text-lg`.

text-xl--line-height.$description: The line height that goes with `text-xl`.

text-2xl--line-height.$description: The line height that goes with `text-2xl`.

text-3xl--line-height.$description: The line height that goes with `text-3xl`.

text-4xl--line-height.$description: The line height that goes with `text-4xl`.

text-5xl--line-height.$description: The line height that goes with `text-5xl`.

text-6xl--line-height.$description: The line height that goes with `text-6xl`.

text-7xl--line-height.$description: The line height that goes with `text-7xl`.

text-8xl--line-height.$description: The line height that goes with `text-8xl`.

text-9xl--line-height.$description: The line height that goes with `text-9xl`.
